prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1365; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The claimant reports a concussion and is not represented by counsel, so all contact is with the claimant directly.

Entry 2: Verified that the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle and that the collision occurred as described. The other driver's statement matches on sequence and point of impact.

Entry 4: Reviewed scene photos alongside the repair estimate. Damage to the rear bumper, trunk, and tail lamp assembly lines up well with the impact described. No prior damage to the vehicle is known.

Entry 5: Medical records show a concussion diagnosis, and the reported symptoms fit the kind and force of the crash. Prior records show a minor strain in the same region years ago that fully resolved.

Entry 6: Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this injury. Requested updated treatment notes and a referral summary from the treating provider to understand the course.

Entry 7: Claimant later provided a few additional details about the event. These are minor, and the core account has stayed the same through each telling.

Entry 8: File reviewed and held for the treating provider's updated notes. No coverage issues identified. Next step is to complete the injury evaluation once the records are received.
